entities.summary:
Adam Odzimek (b. 1955) is a Polish Catholic bishop serving as auxiliary bishop of Częstochowa, the archdiocese historically centred on the Jasna Góra monastery and its venerated Black Madonna image. Ordained a priest and later consecrated bishop within the Częstochowa archdiocese, his ministry has been conducted entirely within one of Polish Catholicism's most symbolically charged institutions.

Częstochowa's Jasna Góra sanctuary—home to the icon of Our Lady of Częstochowa—serves as the national pilgrimage centre of Polish Catholicism, visited by millions annually and closely identified with Polish national identity since the seventeenth century. Odzimek's episcopal service within this archdiocese places him within a tradition of pastoral leadership that must manage both ordinary diocesan life and the demands of an internationally significant pilgrimage site.

His episcopate bridges the postcommunist era's challenges: secularisation, demographic change, and the renegotiation of the Church's public role in Polish society. As an auxiliary bishop, his primary role has been to support the archbishop in day-to-day pastoral administration, seminary oversight, and the management of the archdiocese's complex institutional life. He represents the steady institutional ministry that sustains a major archdiocese's operations.
